extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and IP practitioners filing or prosecuting patents in India (applicants, patent attorneys, in-house counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the disclosure and update obligations under Section 8 of the Indian Patents Act and Rule 12 when the same or substantially same invention is filed abroad; covers Form 3 requirements, timelines, Controller powers, and case-law on consequences of non-disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely submission of statement of foreign applications (Form 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has filed one or more applications at the Indian Patent Office and has already filed one or more applications for the same, or substantially the same invention in other countries, then he must submit, to the Indian Patent Office, a statement that includes detailed particulars ... at the time of filing or within 6 months from the filing of the application via Form 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the Form 3 statement either at the time of filing the Indian application or within six months from filing. This is drawn from Section 8(1)(a) and Rule 12(1)/12(1A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the Form 3 statement (detailed particulars)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement must include detailed particulars, such as date of filing, publication number, status of an application, country name etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the statement lists filing dates, publication numbers, current prosecution status, and the country for each corresponding foreign application. Omitting these particulars risks non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undertaking to keep Controller informed (Form 3 undertaking)
rubrics_metrics.description: An undertaking has to be signed by the applicant, in the same Form 3, which states that the applicant shall keep the Controller informed about the foreign applications related to same, or substantially same invention from time to time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign the prescribed undertaking in Form 3 committing to ongoing updates to the Controller about related foreign filings; this is mandatory per Section 8(1)(b) and Rule 12(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for updates after first statement of objections
rubrics_metrics.description: As per Rule 12(2), this period of providing information to the Controller is three months from the date of the first statement of objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a first statement of objections is issued, provide the required updates about foreign prosecution within three months of that date. Track correspondence and calendar these deadlines to avoid lapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller's use of databases to verify foreign filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Post presenting the information about foreign filing, as per Rule 12(3), the Controller shall make use of accessible and available databases to check similar filed applications in a foreign country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect the Controller to search public/available foreign databases; do not rely on the Controller missing foreign-filed material—disclose proactively and accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to furnish new details on request (two-month response)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Controller may require the applicant to furnish new details related to the processing of the application, at any time after an application for patent is filed in India till grant or refusal of that patent. This information should be provided, within two months from date of communication by the Controller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Controller requests updated prosecution information, respond within two months of the communication. Maintain records of foreign prosecution to enable timely responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include prosecution status, searches conducted, and objections raised
rubrics_metrics.description: The Delhi High Court held that the status of prosecution of a patent application in jurisdictions abroad must be provided in detail, including any information regarding searches conducted and objections raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not limit disclosures to filing dates and publication numbers—provide detailed prosecution history (search reports, office actions/objections, responses) for corresponding foreign applications to avoid later challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in reporting filing dates (national phase vs international filing date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disputes can arise over filing dates (e.g., whether the international filing date should be considered the filing date of the national phase); accurate disclosure of the actual national phase filing date is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the dates declared in Form 3 accurately reflect the relevant filing (national phase vs PCT international filing date) and be prepared to explain and document any differences—errors can lead to objections or allegations of false information (see Nokia case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory nature of Section 8 but revocation contingent on intent/materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: While Section 8 is mandatory, the power to revoke a patent under Section 64(1) is optional; revocation should follow only if the omission was deliberate and material to the patent's grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-disclosure is serious and may be invoked under Section 64(1)(m), but courts have held that revocation is not automatic—intent and materiality will be considered. Keep full, contemporaneous records and, if an omission occurred, be ready to demonstrate inadvertence and lack of materiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principle: prosecute corresponding applications in each jurisdiction of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is required to prosecute his patent application at each national patent office where he seeks to protect his invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan prosecution strategy and resource allocation for each country where protection is sought; satisfying local procedural requirements (like Section 8 disclosures in India) is part of responsible multi-jurisdictional prosecution.
